facts.fact: SPACEBEL says it signed contracts on 16 June 2026 with the DRC Ministry of Higher Education, Universities, Scientific Research and Innovation to supply and maintain the RDC-SAT Earth observation satellite supporting the National Centre for Remote Sensing, which it says will help manage natural resources including agriculture.

note: Satellite imagery is used for census cartography, not farming.

facts.fact: Kinshasa Times reports that the Centre national de teledetection, with JICA, held the first coordination committee of a project to equip the centre to analyse satellite data and supply it to the agriculture, mining and environment ministries.

AXA Climate says the DRC Ministry of Agriculture underwrites a parametric climate insurance product for up to 300,000 farmers in three provinces, to be launched from 2025 and triggered by satellite rainfall indices (TAMSAT and ERA5).

facts.fact: A World Bank-backed parametric crop insurance scheme, whose contract is held by the Congolese Ministry of Agriculture and which uses satellite-derived rainfall data to trigger payouts, has been running in Kasai-Central since January 2025 and began paying compensation on 14 October 2026.
Ecofin Agency reports the scheme's first compensation payments went to 17,180 smallholder farmers in Kasai-Central, with a pilot aiming to cover up to 300,000 farmers through September 2027.

systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture (PNDA), with World Bank, AXA Climate, Mayfair Insurance Congo
